Q: How can I avoid using LLMs as a software developer? A:

Employers "keep(ing) a leaderboard on who is using up how many tokens" is a current trend, where higher-ups demands numbers to quantify "AI adoption", and managers must provide something. If you believe that AI usage does not benefit you, you can surely game this metric - burn tokens for nothing - to get them off your back. There are many such non-sensical things an employer demands - that's just what working for a company means (especially if like me you write software for a highly-regulated industry like healthcare). This is just another one.

If you provide the desired results in good quality and time, then the managers shouldn't care how you got it. Time will tell who provides more value to the employer - you or your LLM-using colleagues.

Q: Can I use the LLVM linker (or related tool) to embed the data from a file into an object file? A:

(An expanded/beefed-up version of @Olonist's answer)

tl;dr: Use llvm-objcopy.

The fact that you can use the linker to do this may be a GNU idiosyncrasy; but - you can definitely do this exact same thing using objcopy - both GNU's objcopy and LLVM's llvm-objcopy. First you need to obtain the relevant target architecture, e.g. elf64-x86-64. This is itself not entirely trivial (see this SO question), but this may well do the trick:

target_format=$(objdump -i | head -n 2  | tail -1)

and now you invoke either:

objcopy --input binary --output ${target_format} foo.bin bar.o

or:

llvm-objcopy --input-target binary --output-target ${target_format} foo.bin bar.o

and this produces an object file with the following symbols:

SYMBOL TABLE:
0000000000000000 g       .data  0000000000000000 _binary_a_txt_start
000000000000000e g       .data  0000000000000000 _binary_a_txt_end
000000000000000e g       *ABS*  0000000000000000 _binary_a_txt_size

Q: How do I do microcontroller programming nicely? A:

You don’t need Arduino for this. Since the project is using an ATtiny2313 with a PS/2 keyboard, I’d use a normal AVR ISP programmer like USBasp, AVRISP style programmer, or Atmel ICE if you want proper debugging.

The black connector is usually the ISP header. It connects to MOSI, MISO, SCK, RESET, VCC, and GND. If the chip is loose, use a DIP or ZIF socket adapter so you can place the chip in it instead of soldering directly to the pins.

Microchip Studio with avr gcc is fine for this. I’d test on the real ATtiny2313 early, because PS2 keyboard timing and AVR registers can matter.

And yes, you can usually reprogram the chip after it is soldered, as long as the ISP pins are accessible and the fuse settings have not disabled programming.

Q: Error sending HTML form data with JavaScript front end through Flask backend to MySQL database A:

If you want to send as JSON then you can't use formData but

body: JSON.stringify({ dateID: dateID, week_day: week_day, day: day, rate: rate }),

You can find more in Mozilla doc for fetch: Using the Fetch API

You may also use

body: JSON.stringify(Object.fromEntries(formData)),

like in answer for question
javascript - How to convert FormData (HTML5 object) to JSON - Stack Overflow
